summary: Current main already implements NGRAM overlap state relay. Added regression and adversarial tests for exactly-once relay behavior, but end-to-end NGRAM serving is blocked because pinned sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1 lacks the reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask CPU and GPU operators required by the checked-out source.

tests.what_was_measured: Four focused cases: overlap accepted-tail relay, non-overlap no-duplication, grammar-barrier no-duplication, and malformed corpus-width rejection.
Real MI355X Triton execution for speculative KV index generation across top-k 1/4 and page sizes 1/16; outputs were checked against an independent Python reference and sentinel-protected buffers.
Qualified tiny-Llama source-checkout server readiness and four HTTP/streaming probes on the assigned GPU without speculative decoding.
Overlap NGRAM server loaded the model and entered its first scheduler batch, then failed because torch.ops.sgl_kernel.reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask is absent from the pinned native wheel.
Direct confirmation that the pinned native wheel also lacks reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask_cpu.

remaining_limitations: repository-environment.json records native=null and supplies no prepared native rebuild command; the checked-out AOT source contains the missing operator but the pinned 0.4.6.post1 wheel does not.
NGRAM overlap end-to-end output equivalence remains unverified until a matching native sglang-kernel is built in the pinned stack.
The tiny random Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only, not semantic accuracy or another model architecture.

EAGLE model accuracy, full backend matrix, memory optimization, penalties, SpecTpWorker parity, EP/DeepEP, distributed DP, PD disaggregation, LoRA behavior, and separate-plan-stream performance were not qualified.
